# jwohlwend/boltzsparkPowered by Gemini

# jwohlwend/boltzsparkPowered by Gemini

Updated onJul 11, 2026Commit[`b1ebfc4`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/tree/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc)Gemini can make mistakes, so double\-check it\.![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz Biomolecular Prediction provides models and tools to infer molecular structures, their binding affinities, and confidence in those predictions\. This software takes diverse biomolecular input data and generates predictions for protein folding, ligand binding, and other complex molecular interactions\.

 The system manages biomolecular data from various formats, processing it through stages of parsing, filtering, and featurization\. This includes generating Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) and handling molecular symmetries to prepare input for models\. For detailed information, see [Biomolecular Data Management and Feature Extraction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#biomolecular-data-management-and-feature-extraction)\.

 Boltz employs deep learning models that utilize specialized neural network layers, such as attention mechanisms and triangular operations, to process complex molecular representations\. These models are often diffusion\-based, iteratively refining predictions for atomic coordinates\. More information on the models is available in [Deep Learning Models for Biomolecular Prediction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#deep-learning-models-for-biomolecular-prediction)\.

 The models generate predictions for:

 - Biomolecular structures and their 3D atomic coordinates\.
- Confidence scores, such as pLDDT, PAE, and PDE, which quantify prediction reliability\.
- Binding affinities for molecular interactions\. These predictions are guided by integrated physical potentials that enforce chemical constraints during the prediction process\.

 Boltz includes workflows for configuring, training, and evaluating these models\. These cover data management for training, model checkpointing, and logging\. The evaluation pipelines aggregate metrics, assess physical validity, and visualize results\. Refer to [Training and Evaluation Workflows](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#training-and-evaluation-workflows) for more details\.

 Users interact with Boltz primarily through a command\-line interface\. This interface performs predictions by specifying inputs, configuring parameters, and managing output formats\. See [Boltz Command\-Line Interface \(CLI\) for Predictions](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#getting-started-with-boltz-biomolecular-prediction-boltz-command-line-interface-cli-for-predictions) for usage instructions\.## Getting Started with Boltz Biomolecular Prediction

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz is a suite of biomolecular interaction prediction models designed to predict complex structures and binding affinities\. It supports various tasks, including protein structure prediction, confidence estimation, and affinity prediction for small molecules\. The framework emphasizes efficient data handling, robust deep learning architectures, and comprehensive evaluation capabilities\.

 To begin using Boltz, new contributors should set up their development environment by installing the package, managing its dependencies, and configuring local settings for development and basic usage\. This initial setup is crucial for accessing Boltz's functionalities, including its command\-line interface for running predictions [Setting Up Your Development Environment](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#getting-started-with-boltz-biomolecular-prediction-setting-up-your-development-environment)\.

 The foundational concepts of biomolecular interaction prediction are essential for understanding Boltz's purpose and interpreting its output\. Boltz addresses challenges in molecular modeling by leveraging advanced deep learning techniques to process diverse biomolecular data formats, infer molecular structures, and quantify interaction strengths [Understanding Biomolecular Prediction Concepts](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#getting-started-with-boltz-biomolecular-prediction-understanding-biomolecular-prediction-concepts)\.

 The Boltz command\-line interface \(CLI\), implemented in [`src/boltz/main.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py) and detailed in [`docs/prediction.md`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/prediction.md), provides the primary method for performing predictions\. Users can specify input formats, configure various prediction parameters, and manage authentication for services like the MSA server\. The CLI generates output files that include predicted structures, confidence scores, and affinity values, allowing users to obtain structural and affinity predictions efficiently [Boltz Command\-Line Interface \(CLI\) for Predictions](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#getting-started-with-boltz-biomolecular-prediction-boltz-command-line-interface-cli-for-predictions)\.

 The overall architecture of the Boltz models involves a sophisticated workflow that transforms raw biomolecular input into actionable predictions\. This includes data parsing, featurization, and feeding processed data through specialized deep learning models\. The data flow from input to prediction is managed through distinct modules and components, allowing for flexible and scalable biomolecular interaction prediction [Overall Architecture and Workflows](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#getting-started-with-boltz-biomolecular-prediction-overall-architecture-and-workflows)\.### Setting Up Your Development Environment

```
# Install Boltz with CUDA support
pip install boltz[cuda] -U

# Set environment variables for basic authentication (recommended for security)
export BOLTZ_MSA_USERNAME=myuser
export BOLTZ_MSA_PASSWORD=mypassword

# Run prediction using a YAML input file and the MSA server
# The input_path should point to your YAML file (e.g., ./my_input.yaml)
boltz predict input_path --use_msa_server
```

To begin developing or using Boltz, the first step involves setting up the Python environment and installing the necessary packages\. Boltz can be installed either directly from PyPI or cloned from its GitHub repository\. The [pyproject\.toml L10](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/pyproject.toml#L10) file in the root directory of the repository, \([`README.md`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/README.md)\), provides detailed instructions for both methods\.

 A fresh Python environment is recommended for installation to manage dependencies effectively\. For general usage, a simple PyPI installation is sufficient\. If development or modifications are intended, cloning the GitHub repository and installing from source allows for direct access to the codebase\. The installation process accounts for different hardware configurations; for instance, the [README\.md?plain=1 L35](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/README.md?plain=1#L35) option can be excluded for CPU\-only or non\-CUDA GPU setups\.

 The core command\-line interface for interacting with Boltz, especially for running predictions, is provided by the [README\.md?plain=1 L3](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/README.md?plain=1#L3) command, as documented in [`docs/prediction.md`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/prediction.md)\. This interface facilitates tasks such as generating predictions, specifying input and output paths, and configuring resource utilization\. For basic authentication with the MSA server, credentials can be provided via command\-line arguments or environment variables\. This setup prepares the local environment for both basic predictions and more advanced development tasks, including access to tools for data processing and model evaluation\.### Understanding Biomolecular Prediction Concepts

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz focuses on predicting biomolecular interactions, which involves determining the three\-dimensional structures of molecules and how they bind to each other\. This process is complex, often relying on fundamental principles from biophysics and chemistry\.

 The models aim to infer properties like [README\.md?plain=1 L52](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/README.md?plain=1#L52) \(log10\(IC50\) in µM\) and [README\.md?plain=1 L52](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/README.md?plain=1#L52) \(probability of binding\) for various molecular interactions\. This is particularly relevant for tasks like ligand optimization and identifying binders in drug discovery\.

 To achieve these predictions, Boltz leverages a deep understanding of protein structures, ligand characteristics, and the underlying physical forces that govern their interactions\. This includes processing diverse biomolecular data formats, extracting meaningful features from these data, and employing deep learning models that can learn intricate patterns from these features\. The prediction pipeline involves generating Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\), which provide evolutionary context, and integrating physical potentials during the prediction process to enhance the realism and accuracy of the generated structures\.

 The core output of the prediction models includes predicted structural information in standard formats like PDB and MMCIF, along with confidence scores that indicate the reliability of these predictions\. These confidence scores can include metrics such as pLDDT, PAE, and PDE, which are critical for evaluating the quality of the predicted structures\. Additionally, for affinity prediction tasks, the models provide binding affinity values and probabilities\.### Boltz Command\-Line Interface \(CLI\) for Predictions

```
boltz predict my_input.yaml \
  --out_dir ./my_predictions \
  --devices 1 \
  --accelerator gpu \
  --recycling_steps 3 \
  --use_msa_server \
  --msa_server_url "https://api.colabfold.com" \
  --msa_pairing_strategy "greedy" \
  --api_key_header "X-API-Key" \
  --api_key_value "$MSA_API_KEY"
```

The Boltz command\-line interface \(CLI\) provides a unified entry point for performing biomolecular structure and affinity predictions\. It orchestrates the entire prediction workflow, from preparing input data to executing models and generating output files\. The CLI is designed to be highly configurable, allowing users to specify input formats, control model behavior, manage computational resources, and authenticate with external services\. The primary command, [README\.md?plain=1 L3](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/README.md?plain=1#L3), located in [`src/boltz/main.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py), serves as the central function for initiating predictions, as described in [`docs/prediction.md`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/prediction.md)\.

 Input for the prediction process can be provided as [main\.py L301](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py#L301) or [main\.py L301](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py#L301) files, or directories containing these file types\. The [main\.py L301](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py#L301) format is preferred due to its comprehensive capabilities, allowing detailed specifications of molecular entities \(proteins, DNA, RNA, ligands\), structural constraints \(e\.g\., bonds, pockets, contacts\), and optional structural templates\. For instance, ligands can be defined by their SMILES strings or CCD codes, while polymers require a sequence and can optionally include a path to a Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) file\. The CLI also supports the generation of MSAs on\-the\-fly using an external MSA server, or users can provide pre\-computed MSAs\. For more information on biomolecular data handling, refer to [Biomolecular Data Management and Feature Extraction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#biomolecular-data-management-and-feature-extraction)\.

 Key command\-line options allow users to customize prediction parameters\. These include flags to enable inference\-time physical potentials for improved structural plausibility, control caching and override existing predictions, specify output directories, and select pretrained model checkpoints\. Resource management options allow configuration of devices, accelerators, and the number of workers for parallel processing\. Prediction\-specific parameters, such as recycling steps, sampling steps, diffusion samples, and step scale, can be adjusted to fine\-tune the prediction process\. Furthermore, the CLI supports affinity prediction, which can be configured through properties within the input YAML file and dedicated command\-line flags\.

 The output of a prediction run is organized into subdirectories for each input file\. These directories contain the predicted structures in [training\.md?plain=1 L257](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/training.md?plain=1#L257) format, along with confidence scores \(e\.g\., pLDDT, pTM, ipTM, pDE, ipDE\) and, if applicable, affinity prediction results, all stored in JSON files\. Additional numpy files provide matrices for metrics like PAE, pDE, and pLDDT\. The output structure and contents are detailed in [`docs/prediction.md`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/prediction.md)\.

 Authentication for the MSA server, when utilized, supports both basic authentication \(username and password\) and API key authentication, which can be provided via command\-line arguments or environment variables\. For troubleshooting, a [prediction\.md?plain=1 L165](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/prediction.md?plain=1#L165) flag is available to address [README\.md?plain=1 L79](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/README.md?plain=1#L79) errors on older NVIDIA GPUs, although this may impact performance\.### Overall Architecture and Workflows

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz provides a comprehensive pipeline for biomolecular interaction prediction, encompassing data preparation, deep learning inference, and output generation\. The system orchestrates a flow from diverse input data to structured predictions, with the core logic residing within the [`src`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src) directory\.

 The process begins with input data, which can be provided in various biomolecular formats such as PDB, MMCIF, FASTA, A3M, or YAML/JSON\. This raw data is initially processed to extract structural and sequence information, including stereochemical and geometric constraints\. This parsing and initial processing occur through modules defined in [`src/boltz/data/parse`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse)\.

 Once parsed, the data undergoes filtering to ensure quality and relevance\. This involves both dynamic and static filtering mechanisms, which can apply criteria such as resolution, date, residue count, and checks for clashing chains or excluded ligands, as implemented in [`src/boltz/data/filter`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter)\. Following filtering, the biomolecular information is tokenized and cropped, transforming raw data into a discrete, manageable representation suitable for model input\. Tokenization assigns unique identifiers to molecular components, while cropping manages input size while retaining critical structural features\. These steps are handled by modules in [`src/boltz/data/tokenize`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/tokenize) and [`src/boltz/data/crop`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop)\.

 A crucial step in data preparation is featurization, where tokenized data is converted into numerical feature dictionaries\. This process includes extracting features for tokens, atoms, and Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\), as well as addressing molecular symmetries\. MSAs themselves are generated using external services, integrated via [mmseqs2\.py L21](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/msa/mmseqs2.py#L21) in [`src/boltz/data/msa`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/msa), which handles job submission, status monitoring, and result retrieval\. The featurization and symmetry handling are primarily managed by components within [`src/boltz/data/feature`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/feature)\. The entire data pipeline, including loading, sampling, and batching of this processed data for efficient input into machine learning models, is orchestrated by data modules found in [`src/boltz/data/module`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module) and [`src/boltz/data/sample`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample)\.

 The featurized data then feeds into the core deep learning models for prediction\. Boltz offers different model architectures, such as [boltz1\.py L40](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz1.py#L40) and [boltz2\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz2.py#L41), implemented as [train\.py L15](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L15) instances within [`src/boltz/model/models`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models)\. These models leverage specialized neural network layers, including multi\-head attention mechanisms and triangular operations, which are adept at processing complex sequence and pairwise biomolecular representations\. These specialized layers are defined in [`src/boltz/model/layers`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers)\. The models predict atomic coordinates, confidence scores \(such as pLDDT, PAE\), and binding affinities through dedicated modules like [diffusion\.py L284](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L284), [confidence\.py L20](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/confidence.py#L20), and [affinity\.py L34](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/affinity.py#L34) in [`src/boltz/model/modules`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules)\. During the prediction process, physical potential functions can be integrated to guide structural accuracy, as defined in [`src/boltz/model/potentials`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials)\.

 The entire prediction workflow, from input to output, can be initiated and managed via the Boltz command\-line interface, detailed in [Boltz Command\-Line Interface \(CLI\) for Predictions](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#getting-started-with-boltz-biomolecular-prediction-boltz-command-line-interface-cli-for-predictions), with the main executable residing in [`src/boltz/main.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py)\. This CLI handles model loading, data processing, and execution of the prediction tasks\. Finally, the predicted structures and affinity data are serialized into standard formats like PDB and MMCIF, including confidence scores and other relevant metrics, through modules in [`src/boltz/data/write`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write)\.## Biomolecular Data Management and Feature Extraction

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz processes biomolecular data, from initial parsing of various formats to advanced transformations, to prepare it for machine learning models\. This pipeline involves filtering, tokenization, cropping, and featurization, including the handling of molecular symmetries and Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\)\.

 The process begins with parsing diverse biomolecular data formats such as PDB, MMCIF, FASTA, and A3M files\. This conversion extracts structural and sequence information, along with stereochemical and geometric constraints, into Boltz's internal data structures\. For example, [a3m\.py L104](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/a3m.py#L104) in [`src/boltz/data/parse/a3m.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/a3m.py) extracts sequences and deletion events from A3M files, while [mmcif\.py L829](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/mmcif.py#L829) in [`src/boltz/data/parse/mmcif.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/mmcif.py) uses [pyproject\.toml L32](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/pyproject.toml#L32) to process MMCIF files into a [mmcif\.py L91](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/mmcif.py#L91) object\. The [`src/boltz/data/parse/mmcif_with_constraints.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/mmcif_with_constraints.py) module extends this by computing geometric and stereochemical constraints using [pyproject\.toml L16](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/pyproject.toml#L16)\.

 After parsing, the data undergoes filtering to refine datasets for quality and relevance\. This includes dynamic filters, such as [date\.py L8](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/date.py#L8) or [resolution\.py L5](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/resolution.py#L5) in [`src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic), which operate on [types\.py L573](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L573) objects based on metadata\. Static filters, found in [`src/boltz/data/filter/static`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static), apply criteria like ligand exclusion \([ligand\.py L8](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/ligand.py#L8) in [`src/boltz/data/filter/static/ligand.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/ligand.py)\) or inter\-chain clash detection \([polymer\.py L175](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/polymer.py#L175) in [`src/boltz/data/filter/static/polymer.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/polymer.py)\) directly to [types\.py L169](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L169) objects\.

 Tokenization and cropping then transform the raw parsed data into a format suitable for model input\. Tokenization, implemented in [`src/boltz/data/tokenize`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/tokenize), assigns unique identifiers to atoms, residues, and chains, converting them into a [types\.py L772](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L772) object\. Cropping strategies, defined in [`src/boltz/data/crop`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop), manage input size while preserving key structural features\. For instance, [affinity\.py L11](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop/affinity.py#L11) in [`src/boltz/data/crop/affinity.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop/affinity.py) prioritizes tokens near a ligand, while [boltz\.py L127](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop/boltz.py#L127) in [`src/boltz/data/crop/boltz.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop/boltz.py) selects contiguous or spatial neighborhoods of tokens\.

 Featurization converts the tokenized data into numerical feature dictionaries required by machine learning models\. The modules in [`src/boltz/data/feature`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/feature), particularly [featurizer\.py L1122](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/feature/featurizer.py#L1122) and [featurizerv2\.py L2160](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/feature/featurizerv2.py#L2160) in [`src/boltz/data/feature/featurizer.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/feature/featurizer.py) and [`src/boltz/data/feature/featurizerv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/feature/featurizerv2.py) respectively, extract token, atom, and MSA features\. A notable aspect of featurization is the handling of molecular symmetries, which is critical for optimizing structure alignment and minimizing loss during model training\. This is achieved through functions like [mol\.py L231](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/mol.py#L231) in [`src/boltz/data/mol.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/mol.py), which leverages symmetry information to improve structural predictions\.

 The data pipeline also involves generating Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\)\. Boltz uses the ColabFold MMseqs2 API to generate these alignments, as detailed in [`src/boltz/data/msa/mmseqs2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/msa/mmseqs2.py)\. This process includes job submission, status monitoring, result retrieval, and A3M file parsing for single or paired sequences\.

 Finally, [training\.py L492](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L492) and [inference\.py L226](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/inference.py#L226) in [`src/boltz/data/module`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module) integrate data loading, preprocessing, and batching for efficient input into PyTorch Lightning models during training, validation, and inference\. This includes various sampling strategies, such as [random\.py L10](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample/random.py#L10), [cluster\.py L163](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample/cluster.py#L163), and [distillation\.py L9](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample/distillation.py#L9) in [`src/boltz/data/sample`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample), to prepare the data for consumption by the models\. After predictions are made, they are written to standard formats like PDB and MMCIF using utilities such as [pdb\.py L11](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/pdb.py#L11) in [`src/boltz/data/write/pdb.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/pdb.py) and [mmcif\.py L17](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/mmcif.py#L17) in [`src/boltz/data/write/mmcif.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/mmcif.py), including the integration of confidence scores like pLDDT\. Custom writers, such as [writer\.py L17](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/writer.py#L17) in [`src/boltz/data/write/writer.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/writer.py), manage the output of structural and affinity predictions\.### Parsing Diverse Biomolecular Formats

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz processes various biomolecular data formats into a standardized internal representation\. This involves extracting structural and sequence information, along with stereochemical and geometric constraints, for use in machine learning models\. The parsing capabilities cover common file types such as PDB, MMCIF, FASTA, A3M, CSV, and YAML/JSON\.

 The core parsing logic is centralized in the [`src/boltz/data/parse`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse) directory\. For example, [a3m\.py L104](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/a3m.py#L104) in [`src/boltz/data/parse/a3m.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/a3m.py) handles A3M\-formatted multiple sequence alignments, converting sequences and deletion events into numerical tokens and structured [types\.py L469](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L469) objects\. Similarly, [`src/boltz/data/parse/csv.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/csv.py) uses [csv\.py L11](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/csv.py#L11) to read CSV files containing biological sequences and associated keys, generating [types\.py L469](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L469) objects while filtering duplicates and extracting residue and deletion data\.

 For sequence information, [`src/boltz/data/parse/fasta.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/fasta.py) provides [fasta\.py L11](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/fasta.py#L11), which processes FASTA files and interprets records as various biological entities \(proteins, RNA, DNA\) or ligands based on header information\. This function validates the format and then converts sequence records into dictionaries for further processing by the schema parser\.

 Structural data is primarily handled through MMCIF and PDB parsing\. [`src/boltz/data/parse/mmcif.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/mmcif.py) uses [mmcif\.py L829](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/mmcif.py#L829) to convert MMCIF files into structured [mmcif\.py L91](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/mmcif.py#L91) objects, which encapsulate atomic coordinates, bonding, and residue information, including support for multi\-model ensembles\. It uses the [pyproject\.toml L32](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/pyproject.toml#L32) library for low\-level parsing and applies cleaning steps such as merging chain parts and removing waters\. PDB files are managed by [`src/boltz/data/parse/pdb.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/pdb.py), where [pdb\.py L7](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/pdb.py#L7) first converts PDB files to the mmCIF format and then delegates to the [mmcif\.py L829](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/mmcif.py#L829) function for the actual data extraction, ensuring consistent processing\.

 A specialized parser in [`src/boltz/data/parse/mmcif_with_constraints.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/mmcif_with_constraints.py) extends MMCIF parsing by incorporating geometric and stereochemical constraints directly into the [mmcif\.py L91](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/mmcif.py#L91) object\. This includes computing constraints like RDKit\-derived bounds, chiral atom configurations, and planar constraints for bonds and rings, utilizing [pyproject\.toml L16](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/pyproject.toml#L16) for chemical intelligence\.

 The most comprehensive parsing occurs via [schema\.py L941](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/schema.py#L941) in [`src/boltz/data/parse/schema.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/schema.py), which is called by [`src/boltz/data/parse/yaml.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/yaml.py)'s [yaml\.py L10](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/parse/yaml.py#L10) function\. This function takes a Boltz input schema \(YAML/JSON\) to create a [types\.py L642](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L642) object\. It handles various molecular types, computes numerous geometric and stereochemical constraints, and integrates template structures through sequence alignment\. This central schema parsing logic extracts detailed molecular information for each chain, including atom names, elements, charges, and coordinates, ensuring the data is properly structured for downstream machine learning tasks\.### Data Filtering Strategies

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz employs both dynamic and static filtering mechanisms to refine biomolecular datasets, ensuring that only high\-quality and relevant [types\.py L573](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L573) and [types\.py L169](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L169) objects are passed to downstream processes\. These filters are crucial for preparing data for machine learning models, helping to remove erroneous, incomplete, or unsuitable entries\.

 Dynamic filters operate on [types\.py L573](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L573) objects, which encapsulate broader metadata about a biomolecular entry\. These filters are designed to assess properties that may change or vary widely across a dataset\. For instance, the [date\.py L8](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/date.py#L8) in [`src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/date.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/date.py) allows selection of records based on their deposition, release, or revision dates, useful for training on recent data or avoiding older, potentially lower\-quality entries\. The [max\_residues\.py L5](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/max_residues.py#L5) in [`src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/max_residues.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/max_residues.py) controls the overall size of structures by limiting the total number of residues, which can be important for managing computational resources\. Similarly, the [resolution\.py L5](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/resolution.py#L5) in [`src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/resolution.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/resolution.py) excludes structures exceeding a specified maximum resolution, thereby ensuring only high\-quality experimental structures are used\. The [size\.py L5](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/size.py#L5) in [`src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/size.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/size.py) sets bounds on the number of chains within a record, while the [subset\.py L7](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/subset.py#L7) in [`src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/subset.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/subset.py) enables inclusion or exclusion of records based on whether their IDs are present in a predefined list\. All dynamic filters inherit from [filter\.py L6](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/filter.py#L6) in [`src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/filter.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/dynamic/filter.py), providing a consistent interface for their application\.

 Static filters, on the other hand, focus on the intrinsic properties of [types\.py L169](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L169) objects and their constituent chains\. These filters are found in [`src/boltz/data/filter/static`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static) and are derived from the [filter\.py L8](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/filter.py#L8) abstract class in [`src/boltz/data/filter/static/filter.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/filter.py)\. An important static filter is [ligand\.py L8](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/ligand.py#L8) in [`src/boltz/data/filter/static/ligand.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/ligand.py), which removes non\-polymer chains \(ligands\) if their residue names appear in a predefined exclusion list\. This prevents common buffer molecules or contaminants from being treated as biologically relevant ligands\. Additional polymer\-specific static filters are implemented in [`src/boltz/data/filter/static/polymer.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/polymer.py)\. These include [polymer\.py L12](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/polymer.py#L12) for ensuring polymer chains meet specified length requirements and [polymer\.py L65](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/polymer.py#L65) for removing chains composed entirely of ambiguous or unknown residues\. For protein structures, [polymer\.py L104](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/polymer.py#L104) checks for structural integrity by filtering out chains with unusually large distances between consecutive alpha\-carbon atoms, indicative of breaks or errors\. Finally, the [polymer\.py L175](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/filter/static/polymer.py#L175) is a sophisticated mechanism that detects and resolves inter\-chain atomic clashes using a [mmcif\.py L10](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/mmcif.py#L10), applying a ruleset to determine which of the clashing chains to remove, thus ensuring the physical plausibility of multi\-chain structures\.

 Together, these dynamic and static filtering strategies provide a robust framework for preparing diverse biomolecular data, from initial parsing to structured feature generation, for training and inference with Boltz models\. For more details on the parsing of these diverse data formats, refer to [Parsing Diverse Biomolecular Formats](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#biomolecular-data-management-and-feature-extraction-parsing-diverse-biomolecular-formats)\.### Tokenization and Cropping for Model Input

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Raw parsed biomolecular data is transformed into a tokenized representation to manage input size and preserve structural features for machine learning models\. This involves assigning unique identifiers to atoms, residues, and chains, followed by strategies for cropping these tokenized structures\.

 The tokenization process, primarily handled by the classes in [`src/boltz/data/tokenize`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/tokenize), converts a structured representation of a molecule into a sequence of discrete tokens\. An abstract [tokenizer\.py L6](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/tokenize/tokenizer.py#L6) class in [`src/boltz/data/tokenize/tokenizer.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/tokenize/tokenizer.py) defines the interface for this process\. Specific implementations, such as [boltz\.py L54](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/tokenize/boltz.py#L54) in [`src/boltz/data/tokenize/boltz.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/tokenize/boltz.py) and [boltz2\.py L379](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/tokenize/boltz2.py#L379) in [`src/boltz/data/tokenize/boltz2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/tokenize/boltz2.py), detail how atoms and residues are converted into tokens\. For standard residues, a single token represents the entire residue, including its type, chain identifiers, and key atomic coordinates\. For non\-standard residues or ligands, each atom might be tokenized individually\. During this process, local coordinate frames are computed for protein residues, and bonds between tokens are established, creating a [types\.py L772](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L772) object that includes both tokens and bond information\.

 Once data is tokenized, it can be cropped to manage the input size for machine learning models while retaining relevant structural context\. The cropping mechanisms, found in [`src/boltz/data/crop`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop), balance spatial and contiguous selection\. The base [cropper\.py L9](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop/cropper.py#L9) interface, defined in [`src/boltz/data/crop/cropper.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop/cropper.py), specifies how a [types\.py L772](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L772) object can be reduced to a maximum number of tokens or atoms\.

 Two primary cropping strategies are implemented:

 - **Affinity\-based Cropping:** The [affinity\.py L11](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop/affinity.py#L11) in [`src/boltz/data/crop/affinity.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop/affinity.py) prioritizes tokens near a ligand\. It calculates distances from tokens to ligand coordinates and iteratively selects tokens, often expanding to include entire chains or contiguous regions up to a specified neighborhood size\. This ensures that the structural context around key binding sites is preserved\.
- **General Boltz Cropping:** The [boltz\.py L127](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop/boltz.py#L127) in [`src/boltz/data/crop/boltz.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/crop/boltz.py) provides more flexible cropping\. It can select tokens based on a random query token, a specific chain, or an interface region between two chains\. After selecting a query token, it sorts all other tokens by their distance to this query\. It then builds a cropped set by including either entire chains or contiguous segments around the query token's residue index, ensuring that structural connectivity is maintained within the cropped region\. This cropper includes fallback logic to select tokens even if the initial criteria are not met, providing robustness\.

 These tokenization and cropping steps are crucial for preparing diverse biomolecular data for subsequent featurization and model input [Featurization and Molecular Symmetry Handling](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#biomolecular-data-management-and-feature-extraction-featurization-and-molecular-symmetry-handling)\.### Featurization and Molecular Symmetry Handling

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Boltz framework converts tokenized biomolecular data into numerical feature dictionaries for machine learning models\. This process involves extracting token, atom, and Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) features, along with advanced handling of molecular symmetries to optimize structural alignment and minimize loss during model training\. This featurization is primarily handled by the [featurizer\.py L1122](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/feature/featurizer.py#L1122) and [featurizerv2\.py L2160](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/feature/featurizerv2.py#L2160) classes, found in [`src/boltz/data/feature/featurizer.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/feature/featurizer.py) and [`src/boltz/data/feature/featurizerv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/feature/featurizerv2.py) respectively, which coordinate the generation of various feature types\.

 Token features describe individual residues or atomic groups, including their type, identifiers, and bonding information\. Atom features provide detailed properties for each atom, such as coordinates, elemental composition, and local frames\. A distogram, representing inter\-token distances, is also computed to capture spatial relationships\.

 MSA features are derived from multiple sequence alignments, providing evolutionary context crucial for protein structure prediction\. The system generates a paired MSA representation, intelligently grouping sequences to enhance information content\. Performance in MSA array preparation is optimized through JIT compilation using [featurizer\.py L400](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/feature/featurizer.py#L400)\.

 A key aspect of Boltz's featurization is its robust handling of molecular symmetries\. This is managed by utilities in [`src/boltz/data/feature/symmetry.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/feature/symmetry.py), which account for inherent symmetries within molecules, such as identical chains or symmetric amino acids and ligands\. By exploring different symmetric configurations, the system can find the optimal alignment between predicted and reference structures, whether minimizing Root Mean Square Deviation \(RMSD\) or maximizing lDDT scores\. This process involves evaluating chain swaps, then greedily applying amino acid and ligand symmetries to ensure accurate structural comparisons and improve model training\. Additionally, various residue and chain\-level constraints, such as RDKit\-derived bounds or planarity, are incorporated into the feature set to guide the models with chemical and physical principles\.### Generating Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\)

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz generates Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) for protein sequences by interfacing with the ColabFold MMseqs2 API\. This process involves submitting protein sequences to the MMseqs2 server, monitoring the job's status, and retrieving the results, which are then parsed from A3M files\. The system supports both single and paired sequence alignments, offering various options for filtering and environmental database usage\.

 The primary mechanism for this interaction is found within the [mmseqs2\.py L21](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/msa/mmseqs2.py#L21) function in [`src/boltz/data/msa/mmseqs2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/msa/mmseqs2.py)\. This function manages the entire workflow: it submits protein sequences, which can be single or multiple, to the MMseqs2 server\. During submission, options such as [main\.py L473](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py#L473) for environmental databases, [mmseqs2\.py L25](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/msa/mmseqs2.py#L25) for result filtering, and [main\.py L474](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py#L474) with specified strategies \([main\.py L940](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py#L940) or [prediction\.md?plain=1 L169](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/prediction.md?plain=1#L169)\) for paired alignments are configured\. The system handles authentication through either HTTP Basic Authentication or header\-based methods\.

 After submission, the system continuously polls the MMseqs2 server to check the job's status, managing various states like [mmseqs2\.py L202](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/msa/mmseqs2.py#L202), [mmseqs2\.py L202](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/msa/mmseqs2.py#L202), [ema\.py L165](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/optim/ema.py#L165), [mmseqs2\.py L228](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/msa/mmseqs2.py#L228), and [mmseqs2\.py L103](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/msa/mmseqs2.py#L103)\. Once a job is [mmseqs2\.py L238](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/msa/mmseqs2.py#L238), the generated MSAs are downloaded\. The final step involves processing the downloaded A3M files, extracting and concatenating their content, and ensuring the output is correctly ordered according to the original input sequences\. For further details on how biomolecular data is generally managed, including other parsing, filtering, and featurization steps, refer to [Biomolecular Data Management and Feature Extraction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#biomolecular-data-management-and-feature-extraction)\.### Data Loading, Sampling, and Batching Pipelines

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Boltz data pipeline manages the complete lifecycle of biomolecular data, from initial record loading and various sampling strategies to efficient batching for PyTorch Lightning models during training, validation, and inference\. This process ensures that diverse biological records are appropriately prepared and presented to the models\.

 Central to this pipeline are the data modules and datasets, which orchestrate the loading, processing, and batching of molecular structures, sequences, and associated information\. The core logic involves configuring datasets, loading raw input, performing collation, and managing the overall data flow for both training and inference\. Configurations are defined using dataclasses like [training\.py L36](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L36) and [training\.py L22](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L22) found in [`src/boltz/data/module/training.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py) and [`src/boltz/data/module/trainingv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/trainingv2.py), allowing for flexible setup of data sources, preprocessing steps, and model\-specific parameters\.

 Raw biomolecular data, including molecular structures \([main\.py L611](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py#L611) files\) and Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\), are loaded into memory using functions such as [training\.py L85](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L85) in [`src/boltz/data/module/inference.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/inference.py), [`src/boltz/data/module/inferencev2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/inferencev2.py), [`src/boltz/data/module/training.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py), and [`src/boltz/data/module/trainingv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/trainingv2.py)\. These functions handle the reconstruction of [types\.py L169](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L169) and [types\.py L469](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L469) objects from stored files, applying schema variations where necessary\.

 Before being fed to the models, raw data undergoes several preprocessing steps, including [Tokenization and Cropping for Model Input](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#biomolecular-data-management-and-feature-extraction-tokenization-and-cropping-for-model-input) and [Featurization and Molecular Symmetry Handling](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#biomolecular-data-management-and-feature-extraction-featurization-and-molecular-symmetry-handling)\.

 The system employs various sampling strategies to generate [sampler\.py L11](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample/sampler.py#L11) objects, each containing a [types\.py L573](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L573) representing a biological entity\. The abstract [sampler\.py L29](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample/sampler.py#L29) class in [`src/boltz/data/sample/sampler.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample/sampler.py) defines the interface for all sampling mechanisms\.

 - The [random\.py L10](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample/random.py#L10) in [`src/boltz/data/sample/random.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample/random.py) provides a basic random sampling strategy, selecting records uniformly with replacement\.
- The [cluster\.py L163](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample/cluster.py#L163) in [`src/boltz/data/sample/cluster.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample/cluster.py) implements a weighted sampling approach, giving preference to less common clusters or specific molecular types based on their cluster membership and molecular type\. This is particularly useful for tasks involving diverse structural entities\.
- The [distillation\.py L9](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample/distillation.py#L9) in [`src/boltz/data/sample/distillation.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/sample/distillation.py) allows for biased sampling of monomer distillation data, categorizing records as "small" or "large" based on residue count and sampling preferentially from these sets\.

 These sampling mechanisms are integrated into [training\.py L187](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L187) and [training\.py L339](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L339) within [`src/boltz/data/module/training.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py) and [`src/boltz/data/module/trainingv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/trainingv2.py)\. [training\.py L187](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L187) continuously samples and processes data, performing loading, tokenization, optional cropping, and feature computation\. [training\.py L339](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L339) operates similarly but iterates deterministically through all records for validation, incorporating validation\-specific logic such as [training\.py L60](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L60)\.

 For efficient model input, individual processed samples are combined into batches using custom [training\.py L144](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L144) functions, found in [`src/boltz/data/module/inference.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/inference.py), [`src/boltz/data/module/inferencev2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/inferencev2.py), [`src/boltz/data/module/training.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py), and [`src/boltz/data/module/trainingv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/trainingv2.py)\. These functions handle padding for tensors with varying shapes to ensure consistent dimensions within a batch, while selectively excluding certain keys that contain non\-tensor data or require special handling\.

 The entire data pipeline is integrated with PyTorch Lightning through [training\.py L492](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L492) implementations such as [inference\.py L226](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/inference.py#L226) in [`src/boltz/data/module/inference.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/inference.py), [inferencev2\.py L317](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/inferencev2.py#L317) in [`src/boltz/data/module/inferencev2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/inferencev2.py), and [training\.py L492](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L492) in [`src/boltz/data/module/training.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py) and [`src/boltz/data/module/trainingv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/trainingv2.py)\. These modules provide [training\.py L653](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L653), [training\.py L671](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/training.py#L671), and [inference\.py L252](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/inference.py#L252) methods, along with [inference\.py L276](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/module/inference.py#L276) for efficient GPU transfer of tensor data, ensuring that the data is ready for model training and inference\.### Writing Predictions to Standard Formats

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz serializes predicted structures and affinity data into industry\-standard PDB and MMCIF formats, integrating confidence scores such as pLDDT\. This process is managed by custom prediction writers designed for PyTorch Lightning, which handle the output of both structural and affinity predictions\.

 The [writer\.py L17](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/writer.py#L17) in [`src/boltz/data/write/writer.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/writer.py) is responsible for saving predicted molecular structures and their associated confidence metrics\. It processes the model's prediction dictionaries, extracting atomic coordinates, masks, and confidence scores\. This writer then updates original structural information with these predicted values and generates [writer\.py L163](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/writer.py#L163) or [training\.md?plain=1 L257](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/training.md?plain=1#L257) files using dedicated functions like [pdb\.py L11](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/pdb.py#L11) and [mmcif\.py L17](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/mmcif.py#L17)\. These generated files can optionally include pLDDT scores as B\-factors, providing a standardized way to represent model confidence within the structural data\. Beyond structures, [writer\.py L17](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/writer.py#L17) can also save confidence summaries in JSON format, detailing various metrics such as pLDDT, predicted alignment error \(PAE\), and predicted distance error \(PDE\), and can save structural embeddings as [main\.py L611](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py#L611) files for further analysis\.

 For affinity predictions, the [writer\.py L270](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/writer.py#L270) in [`src/boltz/data/write/writer.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/writer.py) focuses on extracting and saving affinity values\. This writer pulls predicted affinity values and probabilities from the model's output and stores them in JSON files, allowing for a structured record of interaction strengths\.

 The actual formatting into PDB and MMCIF strings is handled by separate modules\. The [pdb\.py L11](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/pdb.py#L11) function in [`src/boltz/data/write/pdb.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/pdb.py) converts a [types\.py L169](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L169) object into a PDB\-formatted string, carefully adhering to the strict columnar requirements of the format\. This includes processing atoms, residues, and bonds, and mapping pLDDT scores to B\-factor values\. Similarly, the [mmcif\.py L17](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/mmcif.py#L17) function in [`src/boltz/data/write/mmcif.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/write/mmcif.py) converts a [types\.py L169](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/types.py#L169) object into an MMCIF\-formatted string, leveraging the [pyproject\.toml L25](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/pyproject.toml#L25) library to construct the data model and integrate pLDDT scores\.

 These writers are integrated into PyTorch Lightning's prediction workflow, ensuring that as models generate predictions, the results are systematically saved in formats suitable for downstream analysis, visualization, and comparison with other biomolecular data\.## Deep Learning Models for Biomolecular Prediction

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Boltz repository develops deep learning models for biomolecular prediction tasks, including structure, confidence, and affinity prediction\. The core models, [boltz1\.py L40](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz1.py#L40) and [boltz2\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz2.py#L41), are implemented as [train\.py L15](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L15)s to manage training and evaluation workflows\. These models utilize specialized neural network components designed for processing complex molecular representations, such as multi\-head attention mechanisms and triangular operations\.

 A significant part of the architecture relies on processing sequential and pairwise relationships within biomolecules\. Neural network layers located in [`src/boltz/model/layers`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers) are central to this, providing mechanisms like multi\-head attention with pairwise biases \([attention\.py L8](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/attention.py#L8) in [`src/boltz/model/layers/attention.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/attention.py)\), which integrate both sequence and pairwise information for contextual understanding\. Triangular multiplication \([triangular\_mult\.py L39](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_mult.py#L39), [triangular\_mult\.py L127](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_mult.py#L127) in [`src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_mult.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_mult.py)\) and triangular attention \([attention\.py L183](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/attention.py#L183), [attention\.py L186](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/attention.py#L186) in [`src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention)\) are used for efficiently updating pairwise representations\. These operations are crucial for architectures that model complex spatial relationships\.

 The overall model architectures, such as those found in [`src/boltz/model/models`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models), integrate these specialized layers into larger modules\. For instance, [boltz1\.py L40](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz1.py#L40) focuses on structure prediction using an [diffusion\.py L284](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L284) module and confidence estimation via a [confidence\.py L20](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/confidence.py#L20)\. [boltz2\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz2.py#L41) extends this by incorporating features for binding affinity prediction with an [affinity\.py L34](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/affinity.py#L34) and can leverage template information through a [trunkv2\.py L211](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunkv2.py#L211)\. Both models employ sophisticated optimization strategies like recycling, which iteratively refines predictions, and utilize [boltz1\.py L201](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz1.py#L201) for performance enhancement\.

 Beyond the core architecture, the models incorporate modules for generating 3D atomic coordinates through diffusion processes, which are detailed in [`src/boltz/model/modules`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules)\. These [diffusion\.py L284](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L284) and [diffusion\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L41) components predict atomic positions by denoising initial configurations, integrating conditioning information, and using physical potential guidance to improve structural accuracy\. Confidence and affinity prediction modules, also within [`src/boltz/model/modules`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules), take refined sequence and pairwise representations to output metrics like pLDDT, PAE, PDE, pTM, and binding affinity values\.

 Training these models involves a suite of loss functions described in [`src/boltz/model/loss`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/loss)\. These losses include b\-factor, various confidence metrics \(pLDDT, PDE, PAE, resolved\), distogram, and diffusion\-based losses, each designed to capture specific aspects of biomolecular prediction\. The mathematical formulations of these loss functions are tailored to handle molecular context and masking effectively, guiding the model toward accurate predictions\.

 The models also integrate physical and chemical potentials, defined within [`src/boltz/model/potentials`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials)\. These potentials, such as distance, dihedral, and VDW overlap, compute energy and gradients from molecular configurations, providing a mechanism to guide the structural prediction process towards physically plausible outcomes\. Their parameters can be scheduled over time to dynamically influence the model during training\.

 Optimization during training is further enhanced by strategies defined in [`src/boltz/model/optim`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/optim)\. These include Exponential Moving Averaging \(EMA\), implemented as a PyTorch Lightning [ema\.py L9](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/optim/ema.py#L9), which stabilizes training and improves generalization by maintaining an averaged set of model weights\. Additionally, a custom [scheduler\.py L4](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/optim/scheduler.py#L4) is used for managing learning rates through distinct phases of warmup, plateau, and exponential decay\.### Boltz1 and Boltz2: Core Model Architectures

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz utilizes two primary model architectures, [boltz1\.py L40](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz1.py#L40) and [boltz2\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz2.py#L41), both implemented as [train\.py L15](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L15)s in the [`src/boltz/model/models`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models) directory\. These models are designed for biomolecular prediction tasks, including structure prediction, confidence estimation, and, in the case of [boltz2\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz2.py#L41), binding affinity prediction\. They follow a modular design, integrating specialized neural network components to process diverse biomolecular data representations\.

 [boltz1\.py L40](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz1.py#L40) \([`src/boltz/model/models/boltz1.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz1.py)\) focuses on generating 3D atomic coordinates and estimating the confidence of these predictions\. It employs an [diffusion\.py L284](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L284) module for structure generation and a [confidence\.py L20](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/confidence.py#L20) for metrics like Predicted Local Distance Difference Test \(pLDDT\) and Predicted Alignment Error \(PAE\)\. Its architecture processes input features through an [trunk\.py L24](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunk.py#L24), [encoders\.py L45](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/encoders.py#L45), an [trunk\.py L116](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunk.py#L116) \(Multiple Sequence Alignment\), and a [trunk\.py L424](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunk.py#L424) to refine sequence and pairwise representations\. A [trunk\.py L656](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunk.py#L656) also predicts inter\-residue distance distributions\. The model supports recycling, an iterative refinement process where intermediate representations are fed back into the model to improve predictions\.
