Optimization strategies include the Adam optimizer, an [scheduler\.py L4](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/optim/scheduler.py#L4) for managing learning rates, and [boltz1\.py L201](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz1.py#L201) for performance acceleration of key modules like [trunk\.py L424](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunk.py#L424) and [confidence\.py L20](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/confidence.py#L20)\. [Training Optimization: EMA and Learning Rate Scheduling](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#deep-learning-models-for-biomolecular-prediction-training-optimization-ema-and-learning-rate-scheduling) provides further details on optimization\.

 [boltz2\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz2.py#L41) \([`src/boltz/model/models/boltz2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz2.py)\) extends [boltz1\.py L40](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz1.py#L40) by incorporating enhanced feature processing capabilities and additional prediction modules\. It can integrate template information via a [trunkv2\.py L211](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunkv2.py#L211) and includes a [trunkv2\.py L761](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunkv2.py#L761) for b\-factor prediction\. A significant addition in [boltz2\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz2.py#L41) is the [affinity\.py L34](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/affinity.py#L34) for predicting protein\-ligand binding affinity, allowing it to perform tasks beyond structural prediction\. Its processing pipeline similarly refines sequence and pairwise representations through a "pairwise stack" that includes [trunkv2\.py L211](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunkv2.py#L211), [trunk\.py L116](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunk.py#L116), and [trunk\.py L424](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunk.py#L424)\. The [diffusion\.py L284](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L284) module for structure generation is conditioned by these refined representations\. [boltz2\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz2.py#L41) emphasizes detailed logging, leverages [bfactor\.py L24](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/loss/bfactor.py#L24) for mixed\-precision training, and extensively uses [boltz1\.py L201](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz1.py#L201) across various modules for performance\. Both models manage their training, validation, and inference loops as [train\.py L15](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L15)s\. See [Confidence and Affinity Prediction Modules](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#deep-learning-models-for-biomolecular-prediction-confidence-and-affinity-prediction-modules) for more on confidence and affinity prediction\. The architectural components, such as multi\-head attention and triangular operations, are detailed in [Specialized Neural Network Layers for Molecular Representations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#deep-learning-models-for-biomolecular-prediction-specialized-neural-network-layers-for-molecular-representations)\.### Specialized Neural Network Layers for Molecular Representations

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz employs a set of specialized neural network layers designed to process complex biomolecular representations efficiently, focusing on multi\-head attention with pairwise biases, triangular multiplication, and triangular attention\. These layers are fundamental for extracting meaningful relationships from sequence and pairwise data, critical for tasks like biomolecular prediction\.

 Multi\-head attention with pairwise biases, implemented in classes such as [attention\.py L8](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/attention.py#L8) \([`src/boltz/model/layers/attention.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/attention.py)\) and [attention\.py L8](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/attention.py#L8) \([`src/boltz/model/layers/attentionv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/attentionv2.py)\), enhances standard self\-attention by integrating pairwise features directly into the attention score calculation\. This allows the model to leverage both individual sequence characteristics and the relationships between pairs of elements, providing a richer contextual understanding\. A gating mechanism is also used within these attention layers, allowing the model to selectively modulate the information flow\. To manage memory and computational resources, especially for large models or batch sizes, these layers can utilize caching mechanisms and operate within [bfactor\.py L24](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/loss/bfactor.py#L24) for mixed\-precision training\.

 Triangular multiplication, provided by [triangular\_mult\.py L39](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_mult.py#L39) and [triangular\_mult\.py L127](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_mult.py#L127) \([`src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_mult.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_mult.py)\), performs multiplicative updates on 3D data structures\. These operations are distinguished by their "outgoing" or "incoming" interpretation, allowing for interactions between features within a triangular context\. The design includes both pure PyTorch implementations and the capability to leverage optimized kernel implementations for performance benefits, alongside integrated normalization and gating\.

 Triangular attention, detailed in the [trunk\.py L13](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunk.py#L13) subdirectory \([`src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention)\), addresses the processing of relationships within a triangular matrix\. The core [attention\.py L33](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/attention.py#L33) \([`src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/attention.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/attention.py)\) class implements a multi\-head self\-attention mechanism where attention scores are biased by a learned triangular bias\. Variants like [attention\.py L183](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/attention.py#L183) and [attention\.py L186](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/attention.py#L186) handle attention from different perspectives within the triangular structure, effectively managing how information propagates\. Memory efficiency for these operations is achieved through a chunking mechanism, which processes large tensors in smaller, manageable pieces to avoid out\-of\-memory errors\. The underlying primitive layers, such as custom [primitives\.py L30](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/primitives.py#L30) and [primitives\.py L126](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/primitives.py#L126) implementations \([`src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/primitives.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/primitives.py)\), also support specific initialization schemes and [primitives\.py L118](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/primitives.py#L118) precision handling\.

 These specialized layers are integrated within higher\-level structures like the Pairformer architecture, which combines sequence and pairwise representations\. For more details on how these layers fit into the broader model designs, refer to [Boltz1 and Boltz2: Core Model Architectures](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#deep-learning-models-for-biomolecular-prediction-boltz1-and-boltz2-core-model-architectures)\. Utility functions for initialization \([`src/boltz/model/layers/initialize.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/initialize.py)\), dropout \([`src/boltz/model/layers/dropout.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/dropout.py)\), and general tensor manipulation \([`src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/utils.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/triangular_attention/utils.py)\) support these core layers, ensuring efficient and stable operation\.### Diffusion\-based Atomic Coordinate Prediction

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz employs a diffusion\-based approach for predicting atomic coordinates, a technique that frames structure prediction as an iterative denoising process\. The core of this system involves two main components: [diffusion\.py L284](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L284) and [diffusion\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L41)\.

 The [diffusion\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L41), primarily defined in [`src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py) and [`src/boltz/model/modules/diffusionv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusionv2.py), acts as the neural network responsible for predicting the denoised atomic coordinates from a noisy input\. This module integrates various conditioning signals to guide its predictions\. These signals include [diffusion\.py L114](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L114) and [affinity\.py L60](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/affinity.py#L60) \(from [`src/boltz/model/modules/encoders.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/encoders.py) and [`src/boltz/model/modules/encodersv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/encodersv2.py)\), which process sequence\-level and pairwise residue\-level information, respectively\. Atom\-level features and noisy coordinates are processed by [trunk\.py L71](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/trunk.py#L71) \(also from [`src/boltz/model/modules/encoders.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/encoders.py) and [`src/boltz/model/modules/encodersv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/encodersv2.py)\), which aggregates information into coarse\-grained tokens\. A [diffusion\.py L145](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L145) \(defined in [`src/boltz/model/modules/transformers.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/transformers.py) and [`src/boltz/model/modules/transformersv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/transformersv2.py)\) then refines these token representations using self\-attention\. Finally, an [diffusion\.py L157](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L157) \(from [`src/boltz/model/modules/encoders.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/encoders.py) and [`src/boltz/model/modules/encodersv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/encodersv2.py)\) translates the refined token activations back to atom\-level updates, predicting the change in atomic coordinates\. The process also incorporates specific preconditioning techniques \(like [diffusion\.py L392](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L392), [diffusion\.py L395](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L395), [diffusion\.py L398](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L398), [diffusion\.py L401](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L401)\) to enhance training stability across different noise levels\.

 The [diffusion\.py L284](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L284) class, implemented in [`src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py) and [`src/boltz/model/modules/diffusionv2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusionv2.py), orchestrates the entire diffusion process\. During training, it samples noise, adds it to ground\-truth atomic coordinates, and calculates a loss by comparing the denoised predictions from the [diffusion\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L41) to the aligned ground truth\. This loss calculation incorporates weighted Mean Squared Error \(MSE\) and, optionally, a smooth lDDT loss\. For sampling, [diffusion\.py L284](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/diffusion.py#L284) iteratively denoises an initial set of random coordinates over multiple steps, producing a final predicted structure\. This iterative process can be guided by external physical potentials, defined in [Physical Potentials for Structural Guidance](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#deep-learning-models-for-biomolecular-prediction-physical-potentials-for-structural-guidance)\. These potentials compute energy and gradients, which are then used to steer the diffusion process towards physically plausible configurations, improving the structural accuracy of the predictions\. The sampling process also includes mechanisms for coordinate augmentation, ensuring rotational and translational invariance in the generated structures\.### Confidence and Affinity Prediction Modules

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [confidence\.py L20](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/confidence.py#L20) and [affinity\.py L34](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/affinity.py#L34) are central components in Boltz for evaluating and predicting critical biomolecular properties\. These modules process refined representations of biomolecules to output metrics such as pLDDT, PAE, PDE, pTM, ipTM, and binding affinity values, which are crucial for assessing the quality of predicted structures and their interactions\.

 The [confidence\.py L20](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/confidence.py#L20), primarily implemented in [`src/boltz/model/modules/confidence.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/confidence.py) and [`src/boltz/model/modules/confidencev2.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/confidencev2.py), takes sequence and pairwise representations, along with predicted atomic coordinates, to estimate confidence\. It can optionally mimic the full protein folding "trunk" model, allowing it to process inputs similarly to how a primary structure prediction model would\. The [confidence\.py L337](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/confidence.py#L337) sub\-module within the [confidence\.py L20](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/confidence.py#L20) then generates various logits for pLDDT \(Predicted Local Distance Difference Test\), PAE \(Predicted Aligned Error\), PDE \(Predicted Distance Error\), and resolved states\. These logits are converted into aggregated metrics using utility functions like [confidence\_utils\.py L115](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/confidence_utils.py#L115) and [confidence\_utils\.py L135](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/confidence_utils.py#L135) from [`src/boltz/model/modules/confidence_utils.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/confidence_utils.py), providing a comprehensive view of prediction reliability at both complex and interface levels\.

 For predicting molecular binding strength, the [affinity\.py L34](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/affinity.py#L34), defined in [`src/boltz/model/modules/affinity.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/affinity.py), refines pairwise representations and uses specialized "affinity heads" to predict binding affinity values, scores, and binary logits\. This module utilizes Gaussian smearing to convert distances into feature vectors and employs [encoders\.py L209](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/encoders.py#L209) and [pairformer\.py L272](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/layers/pairformer.py#L272) to refine representations before making affinity predictions\. The [affinity\.py L142](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/modules/affinity.py#L142) component aggregates features over masked pairwise interactions to generate the final affinity predictions\.### Loss Functions for Biomolecular Prediction Tasks

| Loss Function | Category | Purpose | Characteristics |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bfactor\_loss\_fn | B\-factor Loss | Measures accuracy of predicted B\-factors\. | Uses one\-hot encoding and log\-softmax on binned B\-factor values\. |
| confidence\_loss | Confidence Estimation | Aggregates individual confidence losses \(pLDDT, PDE, Resolved, PAE\) for overall model confidence\. | Can include relative confidence supervision; supports token\-level or atom\-level confidence\. |
| resolved\_loss | Confidence Estimation | Measures how well the model predicts resolved atoms\. | Uses binary classification with log\-softmax, adaptable for token or atom level\. |
| plddt\_loss | Confidence Estimation | Measures local distance difference test \(pLDDT\) for structural accuracy\. | Compares predicted and true distances with a distance cutoff; uses binned classification with log\-softmax\. |
| pde\_loss | Confidence Estimation | Measures predicted distance error \(PDE\)\. | Compares predicted and true pairwise token distances; uses binned classification with log\-softmax\. |
| pae\_loss | Confidence Estimation | Measures predicted aligned error \(PAE\) between predicted and true structures\. | Computes error in a local frame of reference; uses binned classification with log\-softmax\. |
| weighted\_rigid\_align | Diffusion\-based Coordinate Prediction | Aligns predicted and true coordinates using a weighted rigid transformation\. | Utilizes SVD for rotation matrix calculation; handles variable lengths with masking\. |
| smooth\_lddt\_loss | Diffusion\-based Coordinate Prediction | Smooth approximation of lDDT for coordinate prediction\. | Uses sigmoid smoothing of distance differences; different cutoffs for nucleic acids and other molecules\. |
| distogram\_loss | Distogram Loss | Measures the accuracy of predicted inter\-residue distance histograms\. | Compares predicted and true distograms using log\-softmax; supports aggregation or per\-conformer evaluation\. |

Boltz employs a comprehensive suite of loss functions to guide the training of its biomolecular prediction models\. These losses are designed to evaluate various aspects of structural and interaction accuracy, often incorporating specific handling for molecular context, masking, and numerical stability\.

 A key set of losses focuses on **confidence estimation**, which assesses how well the model predicts the reliability of its structural outputs\. These include:

 - **pLDDT Loss**: This measures the accuracy of predicted local distance difference test scores, which quantify local structural similarity\. It relies on comparing inter\-atomic distances between predicted and true structures, often employing a binned classification approach for continuous values\.
- **PDE Loss**: This quantifies the predicted distance error, evaluating the accuracy of all\-to\-all token\-level distances between predicted and true molecular components\.
- **PAE Loss**: The predicted alignment error loss assesses the model's ability to predict coordinates accurately within local frames of reference\. This involves complex geometric transformations to express coordinates in a consistent local coordinate system\.
- **Resolved Loss**: This is a classification loss that determines whether a given atom or residue is predicted to be "resolved," meaning its coordinates are well\-defined\. Many of these confidence losses leverage a "relative confidence supervision" technique, encouraging consistent confidence ranking across different samples from a diffusion process\. The mathematical formulation often involves discretizing continuous error values into bins and then applying a cross\-entropy\-like loss\.

 For **diffusion\-based coordinate prediction**, a specialized set of losses is used:

 - **Smoothed lDDT Loss**: This differentiable loss function assesses the accuracy of predicted atomic coordinates by comparing inter\-atomic distances in the predicted structure to those in the true structure\. It uses a sigmoid\-based smoothing approach at multiple distance thresholds to create a continuous and differentiable approximation of the lDDT score, making it suitable for gradient\-based optimization\. This loss often differentiates between nucleic acid and other atom types to apply appropriate distance cutoffs\. Integral to this is a **weighted rigid alignment** algorithm that superimposes predicted structures onto true structures while accounting for per\-atom weights, which is a prerequisite for accurate structural comparison metrics\.

 **Distogram losses** are used to evaluate the model's prediction of residue\-pair distance distributions\. This involves comparing predicted distograms \(histograms of pairwise distances\) with target distograms derived from the true structure\. The [distogram\.py L5](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/loss/distogram.py#L5) function supports scenarios where a single or multiple distograms are predicted, often employing a cross\-entropy\-like formulation by comparing probability distributions\.

 Finally, the **b\-factor loss** guides the model in predicting the b\-factor distribution, which reflects atomic displacement parameters and flexibility in structures\. This loss compares predicted b\-factor distributions with target b\-factor histograms derived from input features, using a masked sum of element\-wise products\.

 Across all these loss functions, extensive use of masking \(e\.g\., for padding, unresolved atoms, or specific interaction types\) ensures that only relevant and valid data points contribute to the loss calculation, preventing artifacts from skewing the training process\. Numerical stability is also maintained through the addition of small epsilon values to denominators to prevent division by zero\.

 For a deeper understanding of the specialized neural network layers that process these molecular representations, refer to [Specialized Neural Network Layers for Molecular Representations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#deep-learning-models-for-biomolecular-prediction-specialized-neural-network-layers-for-molecular-representations)\. The overall deep learning model architectures, [boltz1\.py L40](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz1.py#L40) and [boltz2\.py L41](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/models/boltz2.py#L41), integrate these loss functions during their training and validation workflows\. See [Boltz1 and Boltz2: Core Model Architectures](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#deep-learning-models-for-biomolecular-prediction-boltz1-and-boltz2-core-model-architectures) for more details\.### Physical Potentials for Structural Guidance

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Boltz framework incorporates physical and chemical potential functions to guide the structural prediction process, allowing models to leverage known molecular constraints and interactions\. This is managed within the [`src/boltz/model/potentials`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials) directory, which provides a flexible system for defining various potential types and controlling their influence over time\.

 At its core, the system uses an abstract [potentials\.py L15](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials/potentials.py#L15) class, which serves as a blueprint for all specific potential implementations\. This class ensures a consistent interface for calculating potential energy and its gradients with respect to atomic coordinates\. Specialized subclasses extend this base to represent different types of physical interactions\. For example, [potentials\.py L304](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials/potentials.py#L304) computes energies based on distances between atom pairs, while [potentials\.py L321](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials/potentials.py#L321) and [potentials\.py L366](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials/potentials.py#L366) calculate energies related to specific dihedral angles\. More complex potentials like [potentials\.py L437](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials/potentials.py#L437) \(Van der Waals overlap\) and [potentials\.py L573](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials/potentials.py#L573) enforce chemical plausibility by penalizing steric clashes or deviations from planar geometries\. These potentials dynamically extract relevant information from molecular features, such as atom types or chemical bonds, to determine their specific parameters and constraints\.

 A key aspect of this framework is the ability to schedule potential parameters over time\. This is achieved through [schedules\.py L5](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials/schedules.py#L5) objects, implemented in [`src/boltz/model/potentials/schedules.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials/schedules.py)\. Implementations like [schedules\.py L10](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials/schedules.py#L10) allow parameters to change smoothly from a start value to an end value, while [schedules\.py L25](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials/schedules.py#L25) enables abrupt changes at defined time thresholds\. This scheduling capability is particularly useful in diffusion\-based models, where physical guidance might be introduced or weighted differently at various stages of the denoising process to steer the prediction towards a chemically realistic structure\. The [potentials\.py L670](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials/potentials.py#L670) factory function in [`src/boltz/model/potentials/potentials.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/potentials/potentials.py) is responsible for constructing a list of these potential objects, configuring them with specific parameters, guidance intervals, and weights, often using these scheduled parameters\. This allows the model to enforce chemical and physical rules dynamically throughout the prediction process, leading to more accurate and physically valid biomolecular structures\. For an overview of how these potentials integrate into the overall model architecture, refer to [Deep Learning Models for Biomolecular Prediction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#deep-learning-models-for-biomolecular-prediction)\.### Training Optimization: EMA and Learning Rate Scheduling

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Optimization strategies in Boltz aim to stabilize the training process and enhance the generalization capabilities of its deep learning models\. This is achieved through the use of Exponential Moving Averaging \(EMA\) for model parameters and a custom learning rate scheduler\.

 Exponential Moving Averaging \(EMA\) is implemented as a PyTorch Lightning callback, defined in [`src/boltz/model/optim/ema.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/optim/ema.py)\. The [ema\.py L14](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/optim/ema.py#L14) callback maintains a moving average of the model's weights during training\. This technique helps to smooth out the training process, reducing oscillations and often leading to models that perform better on unseen data\. The EMA decay rate, update frequency, and application start step are configurable\. The system can optionally use the EMA\-averaged weights for evaluation phases, ensuring that performance metrics reflect the more stable, generalized model state, while training continues with the original, actively updated weights\. The state of the EMA callback, including its averaged weights and current step, is checkpointed to allow for seamless resumption of training\.

 The learning rate is managed by a custom [scheduler\.py L4](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/optim/scheduler.py#L4), found in [`src/boltz/model/optim/scheduler.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/optim/scheduler.py)\. This scheduler provides a structured approach to adjusting the learning rate throughout the training lifecycle\. It begins with a linear warmup phase, where the learning rate gradually increases from a base value to a maximum value\. Following the warmup, the learning rate enters a plateau phase, remaining at its maximum for a specified number of steps\. Finally, an exponential decay phase reduces the learning rate over time, which helps fine\-tune the model and prevent overfitting\. This multi\-phase schedule is crucial for robust model convergence and is a common strategy in deep learning\.## Training and Evaluation Workflows

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boltz provides a comprehensive set of tools and workflows for training and evaluating biomolecular prediction models\. These workflows cover the entire lifecycle, from configuring training runs and preparing data to assessing model performance and analyzing the physical validity of predictions\.

 The orchestration of model training is managed through a dedicated script, [`scripts/train/train.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py)\. This script employs [train\.py L10](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L10) and [pyproject\.toml L14](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/pyproject.toml#L14) for flexible configuration management, allowing users to define various training parameters, including data settings, model specifics, output directories, and PyTorch Lightning [main\.py L16](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py#L16) arguments\. It supports loading pretrained models, with a specialized mechanism to transfer specific weights to a confidence module, demonstrating an approach to transfer learning\. Checkpointing is handled through [train\.py L16](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L16) callbacks, which save models based on performance metrics like validation lDDT \(Local Distance Difference Test\)\. Experiment tracking and logging are integrated via [train\.py L17](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L17), ensuring that configurations and results are systematically recorded\. For more details on model architectures and their components, refer to [Deep Learning Models for Biomolecular Prediction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#deep-learning-models-for-biomolecular-prediction)\.

 Data preparation for both training and evaluation involves a multi\-step process\. Scripts within the [`scripts/process`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process) directory handle various tasks, such as parsing MMCIF files into structured [mmcif\.py L91](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/mmcif.py#L91) objects, which includes extracting metadata, cleaning structures, handling assemblies, and processing polymer and non\-polymer components\. The workflow also covers generating 3D conformers for small molecules and computing their symmetries, which is crucial for accurate molecular representation\. Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) are processed from A3M files, often leveraging a Redis database for shared resources and parallel execution to enhance efficiency\. A significant part of the data pipeline involves extracting, filtering, and storing structural and record information from PDB files, applying static filters to ensure data quality based on criteria like chain length and inter\-chain clashes\. This ensures that the models are trained and evaluated on high\-quality, relevant data\. Further details on data handling can be found in [Biomolecular Data Management and Feature Extraction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#biomolecular-data-management-and-feature-extraction)\.

 Model evaluation involves a series of steps to thoroughly assess prediction quality\. The [`scripts/eval`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval) directory contains scripts that aggregate various performance metrics, compute statistical analyses, and visualize results\. The [`scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py) script compares different models by computing metrics such as lDDT, TM\-score, RMSD, and DockQ from prediction and evaluation files\. It calculates "oracle" \(best possible\), "average," and "top\-1" values for these metrics and uses bootstrap resampling to compute 95% confidence intervals, providing robust statistical comparisons\. Visualizations are generated using [aggregate\_evals\.py L4](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py#L4) to illustrate performance differences across models and metrics\. The [`scripts/eval/physcialsim_metrics.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/physcialsim_metrics.py) script assesses the physical plausibility of predicted structures, checking for geometric constraints like torsion angles, ligand distance geometry, stereochemistry, and steric clashes\. These checks are applied to parsed CIF files, providing insights into the structural integrity of predictions\. Automated structural comparisons are performed using [`scripts/eval/run_evals.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/run_evals.py), which leverages [evaluation\.md?plain=1 L73](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/evaluation.md?plain=1#L73) within Docker containers to execute [run\_evals\.py L10](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/run_evals.py#L10) and [run\_evals\.py L34](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/run_evals.py#L34) commands, facilitating large\-scale, consistent evaluation of predicted structures against reference data\.### Orchestrating Model Training Runs

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Model training in Boltz is primarily managed by the script at [`scripts/train/train.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py)\. This script orchestrates the configuration and execution of training runs for PyTorch Lightning models\. It uses [train\.py L10](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L10) and [pyproject\.toml L14](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/pyproject.toml#L14) to handle configurations, allowing for flexible specification of training parameters and dynamic instantiation of components\. This setup enables command\-line overrides and structured configuration files, which can define aspects such as data modules, model architecture, output directories, and logging preferences\.

 The training process involves setting up a PyTorch Lightning [main\.py L16](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/main.py#L16), which can be configured for distributed training using the Distributed Data Parallel \(DDP\) strategy when multiple devices are available\. This ensures efficient scaling of training across multiple GPUs\.

 For experiment tracking, the system integrates with [train\.py L17](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L17), which records training metrics, hyperparameters, and other relevant information\. This integration helps in monitoring training progress and comparing different experimental runs\.

 Checkpointing mechanisms, managed by [train\.py L16](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L16) callbacks, are used to save model states during training\. These checkpoints can be configured to save the best\-performing models based on specified validation metrics, such as [train\.py L173](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L173)\. This allows for resuming training from a previous state or for using pretrained models\. The system also supports specialized loading of pretrained weights, where specific parts of a pretrained model, like a confidence module, can be loaded into a new model by adjusting the [ema\.py L77](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/optim/ema.py#L77) to align with the new architecture\. Additional configuration details, such as those related to CASP15 targets, test identifiers, and validation identifiers, are provided through static asset files located in [`scripts/train/assets`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/assets)\. These assets facilitate consistent data partitioning and evaluation across different training runs\.### Pretrained Model Loading and Checkpointing

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The training system within Boltz supports mechanisms for loading previously trained models and for managing checkpoints during ongoing training\. The core functionality is orchestrated by the [train\.py L80](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L80) function in the file [`scripts/train/train.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py), which utilizes a [train\.py L25](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L25) to specify how models should be loaded and saved\.

 When initiating training, Boltz can load pretrained models from a specified path\. This is particularly useful for transfer learning or resuming training from a previously saved state\. A specialized function, [train\.py L77](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L77), handles a specific scenario where weights from a 'trunk' model \(a base model without certain components\) are transferred to a confidence module\. This involves manipulating the [ema\.py L77](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/model/optim/ema.py#L77) of a checkpoint to rename keys, ensuring that the relevant weights are correctly loaded into the confidence module\.

 During the training process, a [train\.py L16](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L16) callback, configured within [`scripts/train/train.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py), is responsible for saving model states\. This callback monitors performance metrics, specifically [train\.py L173](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/train/train.py#L173), to determine when to save the best performing models\. It also retains the latest model checkpoint, allowing training to be resumed from a recent state\. This ensures that valuable training progress is not lost and provides flexibility for experimentation and refinement\.### Comprehensive Data Processing for Training and Evaluation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [`scripts/process`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process) directory contains the data processing pipeline for preparing biomolecular data for machine learning models, handling tasks from parsing raw formats to generating structured datasets\. This includes the processing of small molecules, protein sequences, and crystallographic data\.

 For small molecules, the [`scripts/process/ccd.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/ccd.py) script computes 3D conformers and molecular symmetries from CCD \(Chemical Components Dictionary\) files\. It leverages RDKit to generate optimized 3D coordinates and identify symmetrical permutations of atoms, which are crucial for consistent molecular representation and analysis\.

 Biological sequences, such as proteins and nucleic acids, are managed by [`scripts/process/cluster.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/cluster.py)\. This script categorizes sequences by type \(protein, nucleotide, or short sequences\) and performs clustering\. Protein sequences are grouped using the external [training\.md?plain=1 L132](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/training.md?plain=1#L132) tool based on sequence similarity, while other sequences and ligands are assigned unique identifiers\. This clustering helps in organizing data and reducing redundancy\.

 The processing of crystallographic data begins with [`scripts/process/rcsb.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/rcsb.py), which extracts structural and record information from raw MMCIF PDB files\. This script parses the PDB entries, applies a series of static filters to ensure data quality \(e\.g\., removing poor\-quality structures, filtering ligands\), and stores the refined structural data and metadata\. The parsing itself is handled by [`scripts/process/mmcif.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/mmcif.py), which converts [pyproject\.toml L32](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/pyproject.toml#L32) MMCIF data into a structured [mmcif\.py L91](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/mmcif.py#L91) object, detailing atoms, bonds, residues, and chains, and identifying inter\-chain connections and assemblies\.

 Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\), which provide evolutionary context for protein sequences, are processed by [`scripts/process/msa.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/process/msa.py)\. This script parses [training\.md?plain=1 L236](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/training.md?plain=1#L236) files, often retrieved from external databases, and stores the aligned sequences in a structured format\. The entire processing pipeline often leverages parallel execution to handle large datasets efficiently, with Redis serving as a shared resource for managing data across parallel tasks\. The final output of this pipeline includes processed structures, records, and MSA data, all organized into formats suitable for input into Boltz's deep learning models\.### Aggregating and Analyzing Evaluation Metrics

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Model evaluation within Boltz involves systematically comparing the performance of different biomolecular prediction models\. This process is primarily managed by the [evaluation\.md?plain=1 L73](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/evaluation.md?plain=1#L73) script located in [`scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py)\. This script functions by processing evaluation data from various models, such as Boltz's own implementations \([README\.md?plain=1 L6](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/README.md?plain=1#L6), [evaluation\.md?plain=1 L30](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/evaluation.md?plain=1#L30)\) alongside external models like [evaluation\.md?plain=1 L63](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/evaluation.md?plain=1#L63) and [README\.md?plain=1 L62](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/README.md?plain=1#L62)\.

 The initial step involves gathering metrics for each prediction target\. Functions like [aggregate\_evals\.py L12](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py#L12) and [aggregate\_evals\.py L201](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py#L201) parse prediction confidence files and evaluation metric files \(JSON and NPZ formats\) to extract relevant performance indicators\. These indicators include [mol\.py L270](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/src/boltz/data/mol.py#L270), [aggregate\_evals\.py L9](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py#L9), [aggregate\_evals\.py L9](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py#L9), [run\_evals\.py L38](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/run_evals.py#L38), [run\_evals\.py L21](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/run_evals.py#L21), and [aggregate\_evals\.py L55](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py#L55)\. For each target, the script identifies the "top\-1" model based on its confidence score and records its performance\. Additionally, it calculates "oracle" values, representing the best possible score across all models for a given target, and "average" scores, which reflect the mean performance across all models\.

 The [aggregate\_evals\.py L297](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py#L297) function orchestrates this evaluation pipeline by first identifying common prediction targets across all model types\. It then aggregates the "oracle" and "top\-1" results for each metric and tool into a structured format\. Physical validity data, processed separately \(see [Assessing Physical Validity of Predicted Structures](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#training-and-evaluation-workflows-assessing-physical-validity-of-predicted-structures)\), is also integrated into this dataset by the [aggregate\_evals\.py L508](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py#L508) function\.

 To ensure statistical robustness, the [aggregate\_evals\.py L543](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py#L543) function applies a bootstrap resampling method to compute 95% confidence intervals for the mean values of the metrics\. This provides a more reliable measure of performance variability\. Finally, the [aggregate\_evals\.py L561](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py#L561) function generates comparative bar plots using [aggregate\_evals\.py L4](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/aggregate_evals.py#L4), visualizing the aggregated results with error bars representing these confidence intervals, thus offering a clear comparison of model efficacy across various metrics\.### Assessing Physical Validity of Predicted Structures

| Aspect Checked | Main Function Used | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ligand Distance Geometry | check\_ligand\_distance\_geometry | Verifies bond lengths, bond angles, and internal non\-bonded distances against RDKit bounds, flagging violations\. |
| Ligand Stereochemistry | check\_ligand\_stereochemistry | Assesses the correctness of chiral atom orientations \(R/S\) and stereo bond configurations \(E/Z\) using torsion angles\. |
| Ligand Planarity | check\_ligand\_flatness | Checks the planarity of 5\-membered rings, 6\-membered rings, and double bonds by analyzing atomic deviations from a best\-fit plane\. |
| Steric Clashes | check\_steric\_clash | Identifies clashes between different chains \(symmetric or asymmetric, e\.g\., protein\-ligand, ligand\-ligand\) based on van der Waals radii\. |

The physical plausibility of predicted biomolecular structures is assessed through a series of geometric and stereochemical checks implemented in [`scripts/eval/physcialsim_metrics.py`](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/physcialsim_metrics.py)\. This process validates structures generated by various prediction tools by comparing them against established physical constraints\.

 The evaluation covers several key aspects of molecular validity:

 - **Torsion Angles**: Fundamental calculations of dihedral angles are performed to support stereochemistry checks by [physcialsim\_metrics\.py L15](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/physcialsim_metrics.py#L15)\.
- **Ligand Distance Geometry**: This verifies the integrity of bond lengths and angles within ligands, and identifies internal clashes\. It compares calculated distances between atom pairs against predefined lower and upper bounds, incorporating buffers for tolerance, primarily through [physcialsim\_metrics\.py L38](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/physcialsim_metrics.py#L38)\.
- **Ligand Stereochemistry**: The script checks for correct chiral atom orientations and stereo bond configurations through [physcialsim\_metrics\.py L75](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/physcialsim_metrics.py#L75)\. Violations are identified by calculating and comparing predicted orientations against known constraints\.
- **Ligand Planarity**: The planarity of five\-membered and six\-membered rings, as well as double bonds, is assessed via [physcialsim\_metrics\.py L112](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/physcialsim_metrics.py#L112)\. This involves using Singular Value Decomposition to determine deviations from ideal planar geometries\.
- **Steric Clashes**: Inter\-chain steric clashes are detected by computing Van der Waals radii for all atoms and subsequently calculating inter\-chain distances\. Clashes are flagged if distances are less than the sum of their Van der Waals radii minus a buffer, as performed by [physcialsim\_metrics\.py L146](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/physcialsim_metrics.py#L146)\.

 For parallel processing, the core worker function \([physcialsim\_metrics\.py L248](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/physcialsim_metrics.py#L248)\) parses CIF files and applies these validity checks to individual predicted structures\. Chemical component dictionary information is utilized to provide necessary molecular definitions\. The results are aggregated into a DataFrame, which includes summary metrics such as the number of chain clashes, total pairs, clash\-free status, and ligand validity\. These metrics allow for a quantitative comparison of the physical quality of structures from different prediction tools\. For a broader view of how these metrics integrate into the overall evaluation framework, refer to [Aggregating and Analyzing Evaluation Metrics](https://codewiki.google/github.com/jwohlwend/boltz#training-and-evaluation-workflows-aggregating-and-analyzing-evaluation-metrics)\.### Automated Structural Comparisons with OpenStructure

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The automated evaluation pipeline for comparing biomolecular structures in Boltz leverages [evaluation\.md?plain=1 L73](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/evaluation.md?plain=1#L73) \(OST\) within Docker containers to ensure consistent and reproducible assessments\. The process is orchestrated by the [evaluation\.md?plain=1 L73](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/evaluation.md?plain=1#L73) script, which automates large\-scale structural comparisons by running [run\_evals\.py L10](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/run_evals.py#L10) for polymer backbone evaluations and [run\_evals\.py L34](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/run_evals.py#L34) for ligand\-specific metrics\.

 This script manages the execution of [evaluation\.md?plain=1 L73](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/evaluation.md?plain=1#L73) commands within a specified Docker image \(e\.g\., [run\_evals\.py L12](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/scripts/eval/run_evals.py#L12)\)\. This containerized approach standardizes the evaluation environment, mitigating issues related to differing [evaluation\.md?plain=1 L73](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/evaluation.md?plain=1#L73) installations or dependencies across various systems\. File system access between the host and the Docker container is managed through volume mounts, allowing [evaluation\.md?plain=1 L73](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz/blob/b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc/docs/evaluation.md?plain=1#L73) to process prediction and reference files stored locally\.

 To enhance efficiency for large datasets, the evaluation tasks are processed in parallel using a thread pool\. This concurrent execution significantly reduces the overall time required for extensive structural comparisons\. The system also includes mechanisms to avoid redundant computations by skipping evaluations if the output files already exist\. For the initial task, a warm\-up run is performed synchronously to ensure the Docker image is downloaded before parallel processing commences, contributing to a smoother overall workflow\. This automated system ensures that predicted structures can be rigorously and consistently evaluated against known reference structures, supporting the ongoing development and refinement of Boltz's models\.
